candidate.title: CAB-Seq
candidate.scope: The CAB-Seq (chemical modification-assisted bisulfite sequencing for 5-carboxylcytosine in DNA) row of the assigned Illumina poster: EDC activation, a compressed cleavable-biotin linker interface, streptavidin enrichment/DTT release, and separate untreated-control and derivatized-DNA bisulfite/PCR and sequencing branches. The card and matching collection-page heading identify this target. Neighboring fC-CET and oxBS-Seq rows, cropped text from other rows, and the right-hand biotin structure are visual context, not alternative target workflows or added operations. The extraction preserves the integrated schematic and qualifies its chemistry using Lu et al. 2013; it does not claim that the paper demonstrated this entire integrated route genome-wide or that every CAB-Seq implementation requires capture.

features: The schematic treated pattern is T C C T C.
A C retained at a position that is read as T in the unlabeled control supports 5caC at single-base resolution; retained C alone also includes 5mC and 5hmC and is not a unique 5caC call.

operations.label: 1-ethyl-3-[3-dimethylamino-propyl]-carbodiimide hydrochloride (EDC) chemistry
operations.description: Activate the 5caC carboxyl group within DNA, producing the o-acylisourea intermediate drawn in the poster.
operations.mechanism: EDC reacts with the 5caC carboxylic acid to create an intermediate susceptible to primary-amine attack. EDC is an added coupling reagent, not a DNA product.
operations.information_effect: Creates a chemical labeling handle at a target base while retaining its position within DNA.

evidence.locator: CAB-Seq row: EDC chemistry arrow and o-acylisourea above terminal 5caC

evidence.quote: The carboxylic acid group can react with EDC to form an o-acylisourea ester intermediate that can then be attacked by a primary amine (Scheme 1).

operations.label: Linker
operations.description: Convert activated 5caC into amide-derivatized 5caC carrying disulfide-linked biotin. The drawn Nu–S–S–biotin addition is retained as the schematic input interface; correction linker_implementation explains the primary paper implementation.
operations.mechanism: The diagram shows nucleophilic linker addition. In the primary implementation, EDC-mediated attachment of (4-aminomethyl)benzylazide installs an amide and azide handle; azide coupling with a strained cyclooctyne bearing disulfide-linked biotin installs the capture tag. The paper describes an NHS-assisted coupling strategy; its internal stages are not separate depicted operations. Direct bulky biotin-PEG2-amine coupling failed in the reported screen.
operations.information_effect: Associates a removable affinity tag with chemically labeled 5caC-containing DNA; amide derivatization also supplies the protective chemistry used downstream.

operations.label: Streptavidin pulldown and DTT cleavage
operations.description: Capture biotin-tagged DNA on streptavidin, enrich the labeled fragments, and cleave the disulfide with DTT to release DNA retaining the 5caC-derived linker remnant. The figure combines capture and cleavage in one block.
operations.mechanism: Biotin mediates attachment to streptavidin-coated beads; DTT reduces the cleavable disulfide. Bead attachment is transient within this block, and the output is released DNA rather than intact pooled beads.
operations.information_effect: Enriches labeled fragments, removes the capture attachment, and preserves chemical protection at the target site. Capture alone is a fragment-level selection, not a base-level measurement.

method_scopes.rationale: All seven local operations belong to the named CAB-Seq schematic, including both separately processed readout branches. The upper control is unlabeled input, not a reversal of the lower capture route. The shared bisulfite/PCR and Sequence captions each apply to two distinct local instances. Lu et al. explicitly describe 5caC-specific CAB-Seq labeling, protection and readout, while their capture scheme is a design and the tested single-base readout uses labeled synthetic DNA. The poster integrates these supported components at schematic scope; this is not an interchangeability or universal-protocol claim.

corrections.diagram_observation: The poster draws an o-acylisourea on DNA, followed by one Linker arrow with a generic Nu–S–S–biotin reagent and a 5caC–S–S–biotin product. It does not show an azide or a separate biotin click-coupling step.
corrections.primary_statement: Lu et al. Scheme 1 presents this as a designed direct biotin-amine strategy, but the results report failure of bulky biotin-PEG2-amine coupling. The efficient implementation instead attaches the xylene-based (4-aminomethyl)benzylazide and couples its azide to a strained cyclooctyne bearing disulfide-linked biotin. The candidate Linker operation therefore uses that primary-supported implementation internally while retaining the drawn input, endpoint and single schematic block; it does not assert that direct coupling of arbitrary biotin amines worked.

unknowns.question: The poster depicts enrichment followed by protected and control sequencing, while the inspected primary text reports a synthetic-DNA Sanger demonstration and a designed enrichment route. What evidence establishes how this entire integrated workflow and its matched control were implemented on biological DNA at genome-wide scale? A primary implementation showing those interfaces would be needed for that stronger claim; the schematic-level architecture does not require it.

checks.rationale: Both sides of the discrepancy are present and supported: the poster has one generic Nu–S–S–biotin Linker arrow and a biotinylated endpoint, whereas the primary text calls its direct strategy designed, reports failure with biotin-PEG2-amine, and then implements the azido xylene-based amine plus strained-cyclooctyne biotin route. The candidate explicitly marks this correction and applies it to operation:link. Its activated-DNA input, target-position attachment, disulfide-bearing output, and downstream release route remain coherent; the candidate does not silently substitute the chemistry or claim the complete integration was demonstrated.

Labeling/protection limitations are retained, and the 50–60% value remains explicitly secondary catalogue evidence, with no claim to have inspected the cited Wu paper.
